items.description: Uber’s Legal Redlining Agent reviews contract changes in Microsoft Word using RAG, historical lawyer feedback, and deterministic policy rules. Airbnb Introduces CASTLE for Training Natural Language Search Models with Synthetic Data
items.summary: Airbnb researchers have introduced CASTLE, a framework designed to address the cold-start problem in natural language search. The approach uses de-identified booking sessions and large language models...
items.description: Airbnb researchers have introduced CASTLE, a framework designed to address the cold-start problem in natural language search. The approach uses de-identified booking sessions and large language models (LLMs) to jointly generate synthetic search queries and relevance labels, enabling model training before sufficient real search traffic is available. By Robert Krzaczyński

items.description: The article describes an architecture for agentic AI in regulated utility operations. items.title: GitHub Rebuilds the Copilot App's Diff Surface to Open Million-Line Pull Requests Without Jank
items.summary: GitHub engineers rebuilt the diff view in the Copilot app to handle a pull request with 2,200 files, over a million changed lines and 400 inline comments. The design separates fixed-height code rows f...
items.description: GitHub engineers rebuilt the diff view in the Copilot app to handle a pull request with 2,200 files, over a million changed lines and 400 inline comments. The design separates fixed-height code rows from variable-height comment blocks, which are measured in batches near the viewport. Performance is checked through CI budgets and automated app runs. By Daniel Curtis

items.description: AWS has launched Nitro Sandboxes, running each opted-in EKS pod, ECS task or EC2 workload in its own Firecracker microVM with a separate kernel, enabled by one runtimeClassName field at no extra charge. items.description: A recently disclosed vulnerability in OpenSSH lets an unauthenticated attacker log into accounts that should have no usable password. The issue, named *sshole and tracked as CVE-2026-123158, affects Linux systems running OpenSSH with the musl C library and which don't use PAM. Security researchers now report that attackers are exploiting it in the wild. By Matt Saunders
